text:
Dr. Patel: So, looking at the X-ray, you can see the lower left wisdom tooth here, it's sitting at an angle, pushing against the tooth in front.
Patient: Right. And that's why it hurts when I chew?
Dr. Patel: That's part of it. There's also a bit of gum inflammation around it, we call it pericoronitis. It keeps getting food trapped underneath.
Patient: So, does it have to come out? I've heard some people just leave them.
Dr. Patel: In your case, I'd recommend removal. It's partially impacted, you've already had two flare-ups this year, and it's damaging the second molar. Left alone, that molar could develop decay that's hard to fix.
Patient: What's the procedure like? Am I going to be knocked out?
Dr. Patel: Local anesthetic is usually enough, you're awake but numb. If you're anxious we can offer sedation. The extraction takes about thirty to forty minutes. Recovery is a few days of swelling, soft food, ice packs.
Patient: And cost? I don't have insurance at the moment.
Dr. Patel: For a surgical extraction like this it's about four hundred and fifty dollars per tooth. Sedation adds two hundred. We can do payment plans over three months.
Patient: Okay. Um, I think I want to do it, but can we do it after the fifteenth? I have a work trip.
Dr. Patel: Sure. Let's book the twenty-second. I'll give you antibiotics to take beforehand and a sheet with instructions.

metadata.note: Patient asking dentist about wisdom tooth removal
